items.followUp: Using a velocity–time graph, derive the relation 2aS = Vf² − Vi².

rubric.why: The area under the velocity–time graph gives displacement.
rubric.description: Uses the trapezium area to express displacement.
rubric.how: Award for the correct area relation between displacement, the two velocities, and time.

rubric.why: The gradient of the velocity–time graph gives acceleration.
rubric.description: Uses the graph’s slope to express acceleration.
rubric.how: Award for the correct acceleration relation.

rubric.why: Substituting for time combines the area and gradient relations.
rubric.description: Substitutes for time to relate displacement and acceleration to the velocities.
rubric.how: Award for the correct substituted expression.

rubric.why: Expanding the difference of squares gives the required result.
rubric.how: Award for the correctly simplified final equation.

modelAnswer: From the velocity–time graph, displacement S is the area of the trapezium.
The slope of the velocity–time graph gives acceleration: a = (Vf − Vi)/t.
Substituting in the displacement equation: S = (Vi + Vf)(Vf − Vi)/(2a).
Multiplying both sides by 2a: 2aS = (Vf − Vi)(Vf + Vi).
Using (x − y)(x + y) = x² − y²: 2aS = Vf² − Vi².
